prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1217; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left lane approaching the signalized intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, when the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, whose vehicle was southbound and entered the intersection as the light changed. The point of impact on both vehicles is consistent with a right-angle collision of this type. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder at the scene and was evaluated by responding medics, whose observations align with the force of a side impact of this kind. Passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision and was also present for the statements taken at the scene. Driver 1 stated that no prior damage had occurred to the vehicle. Scene photographs taken by the officer show damage to the driver's side panels and door, which matches the account given by both drivers. No independent witnesses were located at the intersection, and no traffic camera footage was available at the time of this report. Driver 1 provided a copy of the insurance policy, under which Driver 1 is the named insured. Both drivers were cited for further review, and the matter has been referred for follow-up.
